tldr_label: TL;DR: Two Italians die in a drone attack in Kuwait that Iran denies, Zelensky warns of an imminent strike on Ukraine's grid, and futures point to a Black Frida

tldr_bullets.label: Gulf
tldr_bullets.body: Two Italian technicians were killed at an air-defense site in Kuwait. Italy and Kuwait blamed Iranian drones; Tehran denied involvement and proposed a joint investigation. [[TAG:danger:European deaths]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Zelensky said Russia is finishing preparations for a massive strike on the power grid. Kushner said Putin has shown restraint, drawing criticism in Kyiv. [[TAG:warning:grid threat]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: US futures rose about 1.7% ahead of a half-day session, and Asian stocks rallied on strong Chinese factory profits. Brent hovered near $96 ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting. [[TAG:success:rebound]]

tldr_bullets.label: Trade
tldr_bullets.body: China warned it could retaliate against the proposed US tariffs, and the EU demanded Washington honor its 15% deal. Asian allies signaled a preference for negotiation. [[TAG:warning:backlash]]

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Eisenkot signed a second coalition deal, with Yair Golan's Democrats, but his bloc still holds about 48 seats. Katz threatened a new Gaza offensive. [[TAG:info:short of majority]]

sections.title: Gulf: Italians Killed in Kuwait
sections.summary: Two Italians die at Kuwaiti air-defense site; Iran denies drone attack; more mine claims

paragraphs.heading: The Attack
paragraphs.body: CNN and the Washington Post reported that two Italians were killed in Kuwait in what Kuwait and Italy said was an Iranian drone attack on an air-defense site. Al Jazeera reported that Kuwait said they were killed by debris from the drone strike. Yahoo, carrying Reuters, reported that Iran denied involvement, and Araghchi proposed a joint investigation with Rome and Kuwait City. These are among the first confirmed European deaths of the war. [[TAG:danger:disputed blame]]

paragraphs.heading: Hormuz and Saudi Arabia
paragraphs.body: ABC News reported IRGC claims that tankers hit mines near Oman's Khasab, and the number of tankers differs across outlets. The Straits Daily Brief described the strait as effectively closed to commercial shipping. Gulf News reported that the Saudi-led coalition said the Houthis attacked a refinery in Jazan. [[TAG:warning:claims unverified]]

sections.sources: CNN, Washington Post, Al Jazeera, Yahoo, ABC News, Straits Daily Brief, Gulf News

sections.title: Ukraine: Grid Under Threat
sections.summary: Zelensky warns a massive strike on the grid is coming; Kushner praises Putin's restraint

paragraphs.heading: The Warning
paragraphs.body: ABC News and PBS, carrying AP, reported that Zelensky said Ukrainian intelligence shows Russia completing preparations for another massive strike on energy, logistics and essential infrastructure. Kyiv Post reported generators were sent to Dnipro, where the energy situation is most severe. Ukrainska Pravda reported Zelensky pledged to repair damage and respond to every strike. ISW, via Kyiv Post, noted continued US delays in delivering Western-funded Patriot interceptors. [[TAG:danger:winter grid]]

paragraphs.heading: Kushner's Remarks
paragraphs.body: CNN and Meduza reported that US envoy Jared Kushner said Putin has shown restraint by not using nuclear weapons. The Kyiv Independent reported he called Putin a grandmaster of politics and noted his account repeats disputed Kremlin claims. AP, via PBS, said Kushner described talks as at a deadlock over territory. [[TAG:warning:controversy]]

sections.title: Markets: Black Friday Bounce
sections.summary: US futures jump ahead of half-day session; China profits lift Asia; Brent near $96

paragraphs.heading: Futures and Asia
paragraphs.body: TipRanks reported markets reopen for a shortened Black Friday session, and Yahoo Finance reported futures rising sharply in holiday-thinned trade. Longbridge said global markets welcomed US resilience after the AI washout. TradingView reported Asian stocks jumped on the futures rally and strong Chinese profits, and that they shrugged off tariff risks. Figures varied by time of capture. [[TAG:success:rebound]]

paragraphs.heading: China and Oil
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg and CNBC reported Chinese industrial profits rose at the fastest pace in five months, about 20% in October, with AI-related electronics leading. Xinhua credited new growth drivers. Invezz reported Brent near $96.60, on track for its first weekly gain in four weeks, ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting. Admiral Markets and EBC said that meeting will set 2027 output baselines. [[TAG:info:OPEC+ Sunday]]

sections.title: Trade: Partners Push Back
sections.summary: China warns of retaliation; EU demands its 15% deal; Asia leans toward negotiation

paragraphs.heading: Reactions
paragraphs.body: Bloomberg reported US partners responded to the proposed tariffs with anger, protest and diplomacy, with officials from Singapore to Japan signaling a preference for negotiation. Yahoo Finance reported China warned the tariffs could bring retaliation and disrupt trade talks. The News Tribune, carrying AP, reported a proposed 20% rate for China that a US official said could double if talks collapse. World Today Journal reported that China and Brazil led the backlash. [[TAG:warning:retaliation risk]]

paragraphs.heading: Europe
paragraphs.body: France 24 reported the EU rejected the premise of the new tariffs and expects Washington to honor last year's 15% deal. The proposals remain open for comment until January, and the US-China trade truce expires January 10. [[TAG:info:Jan 10]]

sections.title: Israel: Second Partner
sections.summary: Eisenkot signs Democrats deal; UTJ talks advance; bloc still near 48 seats

paragraphs.heading: Coalition
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel and France 24 reported Eisenkot reached a coalition deal with Yair Golan's Democrats, giving them four ministerial posts. The Times of Israel also reported Yashar and UTJ agreed on key principles of a Haredi draft law. The Jerusalem Post reported Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas claimed an Eisenkot government would include both Ra'am and UTJ. Reports put the bloc at about 48 of 120 seats, with a December 6 deadline. Yahoo reported Eisenkot is accelerating talks amid fears Netanyahu could order an Iran strike. [[TAG:info:48 seats]]

sections.title: Gaza: Offensive Threat
sections.summary: Katz threatens offensive and mass displacement; strikes kill 8 to 10 overnight

paragraphs.heading: Katz's Warning
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel reported Defense Minister Katz threatened a fresh Gaza offensive if Hamas does not disarm, bucking the Board of Peace's push. Anadolu and Yahoo reported the threat included displacing about one million Palestinians southward. A separate Times of Israel report said the Board of Peace was encouraged by recent conversations with Netanyahu. No offensive has begun. [[TAG:danger:escalation risk]]

paragraphs.heading: Strikes
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported Israeli attacks killed a senior education official and seven others. AP, via KSAT and Local10, put the overnight toll at between eight and ten in different versions. [[TAG:warning:tolls differ]]

sections.title: Also Watching
sections.summary: Huang faces Congress Dec 1; Cairo tanker fire kills 31; Ebola tops 12,000 cases

paragraphs.heading: Nvidia Next Week
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported Huang is set to face House committees on December 1, the same day as Nvidia's GTC event, and Axios reported the testimony dates. Sources differ on whether the House session is a closed transcribed interview or a public hearing. ABC Australia reported Vice President Vance shrugged off talk of a pardon for Huang. [[TAG:info:Dec 1-3]]

paragraphs.heading: Africa
paragraphs.body: NBC News and Gulf News reported a fuel tanker crash on Cairo's Ring Road set off a fire that killed at least 31 people, and the driver was detained. allAfrica's roundup reported DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 12,000 cases. [[TAG:danger:Cairo fire]]
